fields.features:
PROCEDURAL VEIL- WORK — Sleeping Mystics do not invoke Veil powers by feel, they invoke them by ritual. Each Veil-aligned action you take requires a specific component, gesture, or recitation. You and the Keeper maintain a list of your character's known procedures; new procedures are learned through downtime study, not through inspiration. You cannot improvise. You can, however, combine known procedures in interesting ways, and a strong Sleeping Mystic does so often.

RESOLVE MOVES
Universal · Bear Down: Spend and roll, any number. After any Duality Roll, attack, reaction, or damage roll, before the outcome is narrated, spend Resolve Dice and add their total. The plainest refusal to fail.
Mystic · Ritual Working: Spend dice equal to the power's tier: 1 / 2 / 3. Cast a Domain Power from your one chosen domain, of a level you could normally access, as a sustained ritual: a full action with nothing else that turn (a full round to charge in a crisis), never a reaction, and the Keeper gains 1 Fear as the Veil stirs.
Mystic · Read the Veil: Spend 1. Sense the local register (recent good or evil, calm or storm, recent death) and whether a Threadbender or Veil phenomenon is near.
Veil Walker (School of Path) · Chart the Crossing: Spend and roll 1+. Add the rolled total to a navigation or Veil-transit roll, or shave time off a jump.
fields.a_feattext: Spend 3 Hope to roll with Advantage on all rolls. This lasts until you roll with Fear; when it ends, take 1d4 Stress.
fields.s_feattext: You can spend 2 Effort to choose one effect. The Sleeping Mystic does not bend reality directly; they invoke a procedure, a method, learned from study, that produces a Veil-aligned effect through technique rather than communion. - The Calibrated Ritual. Spend 10 minutes performing a documented procedure. The Keeper resolves the desired Veil-aligned effect (a small reality-shift, a glimpse, a temporary stabilization) at the cost of some pre-known component or concession listed in your notebook. - The Reading. You take a Veil reading of a person, place, or object. The Keeper provides one truthful piece of information about its Veil exposure, history, or alignment. You did not perceive this; your instruments did. - The Procedure of Refusal. Once per scene, you may declare that an Awakened character's invocation of Hope-fueled Veil power is interfered with by your presence. They lose 1 Hope without effect, and the substrate-feel of the room is briefly muted. (This applies to enemy spellcasters as well as allies; the procedure does not discriminate. Ally Awakened characters may consent in advance to be excluded.)
fields.a_domain_ref: Sleeping characters do not use Domain Powers. Use half-step Effort, Resolve, Honed Edge, Recovery Anchor, and subclass Signature Moves instead.
